tools.name: get_readings
tools.description: Fetch Sunday or daily lectionary readings. Pass date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a single day, omit date for today in tz, or pass startDate and endDate for a range. Shared params: tradition, tz. Use this when the user wants scripture citations or Daily Office readings. Do not use it to list seasons, look up a

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: Fetch liturgical calendar data, grouped by focus: current (today's season and cycle, uses tz); year (civil-year overview, requires year); seasons (season date ranges, requires year); special_days (all named holy days in a year); upcoming (holy days from today or date forward); feast (look up a feast

tools.name: list_traditions
tools.description: List supported lectionary traditions and their metadata (rcl, catholic, episcopal, bcp), or pass id to fetch a single tradition. Use this to discover valid tradition values before calling get_readings or get_calendar. This does not return readings or calendar dates.

tools.name: search_lectionary
tools.description: Search readings when the user names a liturgical season (Advent, Lent, Easter, Ordinary Time) or a feast / holy day (Christmas, Ash Wednesday, Trinity Sunday), not a calendar date. tools.name: explore_calendar
tools.description: This tool name is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Prefer the canonical name. Use get_calendar with the same focus values (current, year, seasons, special_days). Additional focuses upcoming, feast, and context are only documented on get_calendar.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_traditions" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
